thread_title: An interesting yet typical S. leucophylla
breadcrumb: An interesting yet typical S. leucophylla

posts.body_html: Here's a random clone of S. leucophylla from Baldwin Co, AL that I'm starting to like a lot. It's not particularly crazy white like the albas, but something about the veining and how the white goes down the trap a bit makes it attractive. Some S. leucophylla var. alba plants can produce red veining in their traps and look like a regular leucophylla, but then they do their chameleon thing and turn solid white during the fall when mature and under optimal conditions. Not this plant: it's just your every day S. leucophylla. This one won't turn solid white in the throat. Will the white travel further down the trap? Hopefully, in time we'll see. Photos taken 9/12/14:
